title.narrative: Integrated Health and Nutrition Response to Crises Affected IDPs and Host Communities in Seven Woredas/towns of Eastern and Central Zones of Tigray Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtTigray Region in Ethiopia faces heightened vulnerability due multiple vulnerabilities, including effects of conflict that occurred between 2020 and 2022. This conflict has resulted in mass displacement, loss of livelihoods, compromised access to food, and disrupted essential services. An emergency food security assessment (EFSA) conducted in Tigray in February 2023 highlighted that 38 percent of the population experienced insufficient food consumption, particularly impacting the nutrition status of women and children under five years. According to SMART plus survey conducted in December-2023, a high prevalence of acute malnutrition in the region with 15.9 percent of children aged 6-59 months being malnourished according to WHO/UNICEF thresholds. Within this group, 3.1 percent had severe acute malnutrition (SAM), and 12.8 percent had moderate acute malnutrition (MAM). The prevalence of acute malnutrition (proxy-GAM) across all surveyed areas was high at 25.2% based on the Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) measurements. In response to the escalating malnutrition crisis affecting children, women, and other vulnerable populations, this project aims to provide a comprehensive and integrated health and nutrition interventions. Moreover, the region's health system, already weakened by ongoing challenges, is struggling to manage multiple concurrent outbreaks, particularly among IDPs. The proposed project will deliver a robust package of services across health facilities and communities including the establishment and strengthening of Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTPs) and Stabilization Centers (SCs) to provide both preventive and curative care for SAM, deploying of MHNT to provide basic preventive and curative primary health care services for IDPs and hard to reach communities, procure and support medical supplies to strengthen the health facilities ability to provide quality services, supporting the health system through technical and logistical support in responding to multiple outbreaks occurring in the region, making minor rehabilitation for health facilities damaged during conflict to provide the necessary health and nutrition services for the affected communities. Furthermore, ASDEPO empowers local communities and health facilities to take ownership of their health and nutrition outcomes through partnerships with health offices and local leaders, fostering durable, community-led solutions that enhance the sustainability and effectiveness of interventions. This integrated approach also focuses on strengthening health systems to deliver a comprehensive nutrition services, involving capacity building for health workers, improving infrastructure, and ensuring the availability of essential supplies and equipment. By leveraging local knowledge, building community capacity, and inter-sectoral collaboration, ASDEPO aims to create lasting change that extends beyond immediate relief efforts, contributing to the broader goal of ending all forms of malnutrition by 2030. The proposed project aims to deliver crucial nutrition and health support to vulnerable communities in Ahferom, Chilla, and Adwa from central zone and Zalanbesa, Freweini, Kilite Awlalo, Edaga Hamus towns/woredas from Eastern zone of the Tigray region. ASDEPO will support by implementing integrated nutrition and health response, strengthening of the health system in responding to malnutrition and outbreaks. The targeted areas have the highest case load of people who have been affected by prolonged conflict. The project's design aligns with the identified needs and priorities of both the government and humanitarian clusters, acknowledging the increased humanitarian demands in the targeted areas due to conflict and challenging conditions.ltbrgt The total budget of the project is 1000,000 USD. Through this budget the project will directly reach 165,256 people in need in the targeted woredas of which 46% are female and 25% are children as well as 29% are male.lt/pgt
